frequency_question: How often does an announced or contemplated structural liquidity absorption tool (like incremental reserve ratios or special deposit facilities) successfully reach full operational implementation rather than being aborted due to institutional friction?
membership_rule: Includes all formal central bank announcements or pre-announcements of targeted liquidity impoundment mechanisms (incremental CRR, special CRR, or equivalent non-standard reserve freezes) intended to manage systemic surplus liquidity; excludes standard baseline adjustments to permanent reserve ratios.

cases.name: People's Bank of China Targeted RRR Cuts/Adjustments
Reserve Bank of Australia Term Funding Facility adjustments
Bank of Korea Base Rate and Reserve Requirement tightening
Bank Indonesia Macroprudential Liquidity Buffer adjustment

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named; representative of major jurisdictions implementing targeted liquidity constraints.
known_gaps: Excludes minor or unpublished internal central bank deliberations that were abandoned before public notification.
skeleton: Emerging market and major central bank non-standard liquidity tightening episodes since 2010 where operational friction was explicitly evaluated by market participants.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 6 instances of announced non-standard liquidity impoundment instruments reaching implementation.
validity_reason: Central bank operational autonomy and institutional frameworks for liquidity management remain stable over multi-year horizons.
